prep.summary: You synced with Jon throughout late August on architectural boundaries—specifically separating high-level blueprints from lower-level implementation—and tracked critical infrastructure blockers including the Neptune database firewall issue. You also solidified process ownership for PL1/PL2 with directors running triage—directly supporting RV's demand for independent architecture gating before contract sign-offs. No work notes exist for the September 1st meeting with Arvy—known as RV in previous syncs—but his recent directives focus on platform taxonomy, gating, and final CLM approvals.
tasks: Resolve the Neptune data read/write blocker with Tito Warren—Joe Denton remains out on vacation—to free up the infrastructure pipeline.
Deliver the integrated PNC automation capability model and roadmap to Jon—collaborating with Madhu and Ian's delegates—by the end of the week.
Align with RV on the updated PL1/PL2 process ownership—ensuring directors are recorded as formal owners in ServiceNow and Risk management platforms.
Enforce the C4 model boundary—retaining architecture accountability for C_0 to C_2 and leaving C_3 to C_4 to solution engineering—to eliminate team role confusion.
prep.title: Biweekly with Jon

prep.summary: During your last sync with Aaron on August 27—focused heavily on the Intelligent Printer dispute—you addressed Robert Lagutus's push to transfer ownership and its $1.5M–$2M unfunded migration cost to P&C. This forced legacy transfer directly contradicts established platform ownership strategy—an issue Aaron planned to escalate to RV. Meanwhile—following the recent ATS process reorganization—Mike Henry is slated to assume ownership of Tech Strategy under your executive sponsorship.
tasks: Draft the concise Intelligent Printer ownership and funding summary for Aaron to present to RV.
Share the email thread involving Mike Wilkins and Robert Lagutus with Aaron to provide historical context.
Confirm Mike Henry's readiness and transition timeline for taking over the Tech Strategy process ownership.
Review the legacy system retirement pipeline on the Technology Obsolescence dashboard to identify further RBT savings.
prep.title: Mike 1on1

prep.summary: Your last meeting with Sai on May 8 focused on shifting from dozens of small AI use cases to two or three high-impact "Big Rocks" — a critical transition complicated by a leadership vacuum and severe operational bottlenecks. You discussed how the Gen AI Council and Model Risk Management (MRM) review processes act as a chokehold on innovation — especially regarding Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) and vendor integration. To resolve this, you advocated for a streamlined playbook approach to evaluate AI risk in days rather than months while resisting vendor proliferation in favor of existing core platforms.
tasks: Address the leadership confusion left by Romnik, Rachel, and Tina — stabilizing the AI strategy execution.
Finalize the proposed "playbook" risk-evaluation process — mimicking a SOC 2 check — to bypass the lengthy MRM and Gen AI Council bottlenecks.
Push for the consolidated "Big Rocks" strategy — specifically focusing resources on the 2–3 high-impact use cases instead of dozens of minor projects.
Establish clear guidelines on the build-versus-buy approach — prioritizing existing major investments like AWS over startup vendor proliferation.
prep.title: Sai, monthly one-on-one
